headline: Clop, Medusa, and AWS Keys: Daily Cybersecurity Briefing
summary:
This daily summary highlights critical updates and new threats impacting organizations. The Clop ransomware group's exploitation of a zero-day vulnerability in PTC software (CVE-2026-12569) has been confirmed, leading to significant data exfiltration from major companies like General Electric and Shell. Medusa ransomware continues its widespread impact, with an updated advisory detailing new tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs), including exploitation of vulnerabilities in ConnectWise ScreenConnect and Fortinet FortiClient EMS. Defenders should review the latest MITRE ATT&CK techniques and hunting hints provided.

In cloud security, thousands of AWS keys, many with full administrative privileges, remain active and publicly exposed, posing a severe risk of account takeover and data theft. Apollo Global Management disclosed a data breach resulting from a social engineering campaign, underscoring the persistent threat of human-targeted attacks. An Italian school software firm, Spaggiari, has been targeted by the 'xpl0itrs' group, with a claim of 6.1 terabytes of data stolen, potentially impacting over 3,000 schools.

Finally, a sophisticated supply-chain attack targeting the Rust programming language ecosystem has been attributed to North Korean state-sponsored actors. The attack involved compromising a maintainer's account on crates.io to distribute malicious versions of popular libraries. Microsoft has also issued a clarification regarding CVE-2026-69836 in Entra ID, stating it was not actively exploited in the wild, though its technical severity remains high.

articles.headline: Clop Group Claims Massive Data Heist from Shell, Philips, GE via PTC Flaw
articles.title: Clop Exploits PTC Flaw (CVE-2026-12569) in Mass Attack
articles.excerpt: The Clop ransomware and extortion group has listed nearly 50 multinational corporations, including Shell, Philips, and General Electric, as victims of a mass data theft campaign. The attacks are believed to have exploited CVE-2026-12569, a critical vulnerability in PTC's Windchill and FlexPLM product lifecycle management software. This campaign follows Clop's established pattern of exploiting a single flaw in widely used enterprise software to compromise many organizations at once, similar to its previous MOVEit and GoAnywhere attacks.
articles.updateSummary: New details confirm CVE-2026-12569 as an RCE zero-day exploited by Clop before patch. GE data exfiltration updated to 391GB; Shell confirms investigation, core operations unaffected.
articles.updateContent: The Clop ransomware group's exploitation of CVE-2026-12569 is now confirmed as an unauthenticated remote code execution (RCE) flaw stemming from unsafe deserialization. Security researchers believe Clop began exploiting this zero-day vulnerability in early June, weeks before PTC's public disclosure and patch release on June 17. The reported data exfiltration from General Electric has been updated to 391GB, significantly higher than previously known. Shell has acknowledged the claims and initiated an investigation, confirming that its core business operations remain unaffected by the data theft.

articles.headline: Medusa Ransomware Has Breached Over 500 Critical Infrastructure Orgs
articles.title: Medusa Ransomware Attacks Surpass 500 Victims
articles.excerpt: An updated joint advisory from the FBI, CISA, and HHS reveals the Medusa ransomware group has compromised over 500 organizations since June 2021, a sharp increase from previous reports. Operating as a Ransomware-as-a-Service (RaaS), the group targets critical infrastructure sectors including healthcare and defense. Medusa affiliates gain access via initial access brokers and by exploiting unpatched vulnerabilities, sometimes within 24 hours of public disclosure. The group employs a double-extortion model, encrypting data and leaking it on a dark web site if the ransom is not paid.
articles.updateSummary: CISA/FBI update Medusa advisory with new TTPs, including exploitation of ConnectWise ScreenConnect and Fortinet vulnerabilities, and additional hunting hints.
articles.updateContent: The updated CISA/FBI/HHS advisory details new Medusa ransomware TTPs, significantly expanding on previous intelligence. Key additions include the active exploitation of CVE-2024-1709 in ConnectWise ScreenConnect and vulnerabilities in Fortinet FortiClient EMS. The advisory also explicitly lists new MITRE ATT&CK techniques like T1133 (External Remote Services) and T1490 (Inhibit System Recovery), alongside new hunting hints such as the '/api/config' URL pattern for BeyondTrust exploitation and the 'bomgar-scc.exe' process name. This update provides critical, actionable intelligence for defenders.

articles.headline: Microsoft Patches Exploited CVSS 10.0 Zero-Day in Entra ID Service
articles.title: Microsoft Entra ID Zero-Day (CVE-2026-69836) Patched
articles.excerpt: Microsoft has deployed a server-side patch for a critical remote code execution (RCE) vulnerability in its Entra ID cloud identity service, tracked as CVE-2026-69836. The flaw, which has a maximum CVSS score of 10.0, was confirmed to have been exploited as a zero-day before Microsoft's internal discovery and mitigation. The vulnerability stemmed from the deserialization of untrusted data, allowing unauthenticated attackers to execute code remotely. As the fix was applied on Microsoft's backend, no customer action is required. Details regarding the attackers or the scope of exploitation have not been disclosed. A compromise of Entra ID could grant attackers widespread access to Microsoft 365, Azure, and other connected cloud environments.
articles.updateSummary: Microsoft clarifies CVE-2026-69836 in Entra ID was not actively exploited as a zero-day, contradicting initial reports.
articles.updateContent: Microsoft has issued a clarification regarding CVE-2026-69836, the critical RCE in Entra ID. While initial reports, including Microsoft's own, indicated active zero-day exploitation, the company later amended its advisory to state that the vulnerability was not actively exploited in the wild. This correction significantly alters the understanding of the immediate threat posed by the flaw, although its technical severity remains high. The vulnerability was discovered by a Microsoft Principal Security Engineer and has been fully mitigated server-side.

articles.headline: Thousands of Leaked AWS Keys, Many with Full Admin, Remain Active
articles.title: Leaked AWS Keys with Admin Access Found Active by Truffle Security
articles.excerpt: A large-scale investigation by Truffle Security has uncovered a severe and persistent cloud security risk: thousands of publicly leaked Amazon Web Services (AWS) keys remain active, many for years. The researchers found 768 active keys that grant full administrative control, including 526 root keys, which provide the highest possible privileges. These keys, discovered in public code repositories, datasets on Hugging Face, and CI/CD logs, expose organizations to complete account takeover, data theft, and resource hijacking.

articles.headline: Apollo Global Management Discloses Data Breach via Social Engineering
articles.title: Apollo Global Management Confirms Breach from Social Engineering
articles.excerpt: Investment giant Apollo Global Management has disclosed a data breach that occurred in July 2026. The incident was not caused by malware but by a social engineering campaign where attackers, likely posing as IT helpdesk staff, tricked employees into granting them unauthorized access to company cloud platforms. The breach resulted in the exposure of sensitive personal information, including names, home addresses, and Social Security numbers, highlighting the persistent threat of human-targeted attacks in the financial sector.

articles.headline: Italian School Software Firm 'Spaggiari' Hacked; 6.1 TB of Data Claimed
articles.title: xpl0itrs Group Claims 6.1TB Data Theft from Italy's Gruppo Spaggiari
articles.excerpt: The emerging extortion group 'xpl0itrs' has claimed a massive data breach against Gruppo Spaggiari Parma, a major Italian provider of school administration software. The group alleges it stole 6.1 terabytes of data affecting over 3,000 schools, including sensitive information on students and teachers from the popular 'ClasseViva' platform. While Spaggiari has confirmed an incident, it claims the breach was limited in scope. The attackers are reportedly selling the data after failed negotiations, posing a significant privacy risk to millions.

articles.headline: North Korean Hackers Target Rust Ecosystem in Supply-Chain Attack
articles.title: North Korean Group 'Sapphire Sleet' Behind Rust Supply-Chain Attack
articles.excerpt: A sophisticated software supply-chain attack targeting the Rust programming language ecosystem has been attributed to the North Korean state-sponsored threat actor 'Sapphire Sleet'. Researchers at Wiz discovered that the attackers compromised a maintainer's account on crates.io, the official Rust package registry, and published malicious versions of several popular libraries, known as 'crates'. The attack used a typosquatted dependency to subtly inject malware designed to steal developer credentials and other sensitive data during the software compilation process.
